2026-09-13: user bug report questioned fact #7 (the `dies` fact sharing its annotation with the chapter I/II `destroy` fact) — was its value:4 a miscategorization/copy-paste of the destroy fact's own value? Investigated: this card's synergy.json had simply never been run back through compute-weights.mjs since being hand-authored (`destroy`/`cast`/`entersBattlefield`/`sacrifice`/`putCounter` were all still carrying the literal `-1` 'pending' placeholder; `drawCard` was a stale hand-set 4, out of step with the rest of the pool where a plain `drawCard` fact — no dedicated magnitude branch in compute-weights.mjs's `sourceMagnitude` — always lands on the flat neutral 1). Re-ran `npx vite-node functional-model/scripts/compute-weights.mjs --slug=summon-bahamut` (the pool's own sanctioned fix for exactly this staleness class): the `dies` fact's magnitude comes from `Math.max(1, countOf(log,'destroy'), countOf(log,'sacrifice'))` over the WHOLE trace log, not scoped to its own clause — this card's one real scenario has exactly 1 literal `destroy` (Coeurl) and 1 literal `sacrifice` (Bahamut itself via 714.4), so fresh magnitude is 1, value 1 — same as the card's OTHER `dies` fact (the self-sacrifice one, at line 0), which was already correctly 1. So: NOT a miscategorization (the `dies` fact is correct, real, CR 700.4-backed vocabulary distinct from `destroy`'s own CR 701.6 act — Ultima's own progress.json documents the same intentional split) — but the specific value:4 WAS stale, now corrected to 1 via the sanctioned tool. `review` was already `ai` (not `human`), so no reset needed. Separately confirmed the annotation-scope complaint (only 'Destroy up to one target nonland permanent', not the 'I, II — ' prefix) is unrelated to any bug — it's version drift against this same session's still-inert `PRD_AUTOMATED_AUTHORING.md` definition-level-annotation prototype (this card's own `definition.ts` `chapterI`/`chapterII` triggers now carry a NEW, deliberately coarser whole-line `annotation` field including the 'I, II — ' prefix, but that field is confirmed not wired into apply-recognizers.mjs/synergy.json yet) — the live, narrower regex-recognizer-derived annotation (`destroy-effect-structural`, which by design excludes the shared chapter-number prefix) is what's actually served today. Broader pool sweep for the same destroy-vs-dies pattern found 5 more cards whose `dies` value doesn't match a fresh compute-weights.mjs run (deadly-embrace, dion-bahamut-s-dominant-bahamut-warden-of-light, dwarven-castle-guard, fate-of-the-sun-cryst, summon-knights-of-round) — NOT fixed here: their synergy.json/scenarios.ts/trace.json are already mid-edit from a separate, unrelated in-flight uncommitted migration this same session (confirmed via git status — provenance blocks/new facts already present before this task touched them), so touching their weights now risks colliding with that other in-progress work; left for a dedicated follow-up once that settles. deadly-embrace specifically also has a DIFFERENT, deeper issue worth flagging separately: its scenario's opponent creature is `creaturesCount` (harness.ts default token-modeled filler), so its real kill logs as `ceasesToExist`, never a literal `fn:'destroy'` — a bare compute-weights.mjs rerun there would wrongly zero its `dies` value to the neutral floor (1) despite two real narrative deaths across its two scenarios; fixing that one properly needs a scenario-authoring change (`nontokenCreaturesCount:1`), not just a weights rerun.

No real trace evidence possible (static `keywords` data, never a real action call) — covered by a new general verify-synergy.mjs exemption, isInnatePrintedKeywordFact. find-synergies.mjs before/after (isolated swap): 0 diff — real, documented zero-match new vocabulary usage. verify-synergy.mjs (scoped + full pool 314): 0 hard failures; vitest 238/238.

Earlier: User pushed back on the self-destroy scenario ('Why itself!? Not something you would ever attempt.'). Root cause: chapter I/II's destroy pool is [you-bucket, opp-bucket] in that fixed order, self is always in you-bucket with no exclusion, real text is unrestricted, chooseTarget always takes candidate[0] — self is unavoidably first. Fix: made `optional` (real TargetMin$0) genuinely functional instead of documentary-only — new `EffectContext.declineOptional` (card.ts) + `Scenario.declineTriggers` (harness.ts), set per-trigger, lets a scenario really decline a target instead of being forced onto whatever chooseTarget would deterministically pick. The common-line scenario now has chapters I/II BOTH decline (opponent still has a real legal artifact target on board, to prove it's a genuine decline, not 'nothing to hit') — matches user's own resolution ('it doesn't have to destroy anything... up to one, 0 is fine'). A second, minimal scenario (isolated `trigger:'chapterI'`, no decline) keeps the destroy-nonland produce fact backed by real trace evidence (self-target, same legal-if-pointless outcome Coeurl/Dion's own chapter III already documents) — without it verify-synergy.mjs would hard-fail the fact for having no supporting trace line at all.
knownGaps: Resolved 2026-09-11 (previously listed here as an open gap, now stale): scenario A's `EffectContext.preferTarget` override does let a scenario demonstrate chapter I hitting an opponent's own permanent specifically (a real Coeurl, opponent-controlled) despite `self` always sorting first in the unrestricted destroy pool's default `chooseTarget` order — `preferTarget` overrides that default pick, it isn't blocked by the pool ordering the way plain `chooseTarget` would be.

`sequence` fires named triggers back-to-back with no real lore-counter/turn-by-turn tracking — doesn't simulate 3 real turns passing, just 'these triggers really do all happen, in this order, over the game.'

`declineOptional` is new and only wired into the `destroy` effect kind — other `optional`-bearing effects (move/sacrifice/dig) still don't support a real decline; extend only when a real card needs it.
